title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement:
For complex numbers \(u=a+bi\) and \(v=c+di,\) define the binary operation \(\otimes\) by

\[ u\otimes v=ac+bdi. \]

Suppose \(z\) is a complex number such that \(z\otimes z=z^2+40.\) What is \(|z|?\)

solutions.text:
With \(z=a+bi,\) we have \(z\otimes z=a^2+b^2 i\) and \(z^2+40=(a^2-b^2+40)+2abi.\) The real parts give \(a^2=a^2-b^2+40,\) so \(b^2=40.\) The imaginary parts give \(b^2=2ab,\) so \(b=2a\) and \(a^2=\tfrac{b^2}{4}=10.\) Then \(|z|^2=a^2+b^2=50,\) so \(|z|=5\sqrt{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Match real and imaginary parts of \(z\otimes z=z^2+40,\) then compute \(a^2+b^2\)
